# Polynomial calculations supporting Step 5

This companion displays the polynomial operations behind elimination, exceptional cases, resultants and exact root counts. Symbolic algebra independently checks each equality; it does not replace the evaluated background variation in the five step files. Symbols $`a,x,K,Q,S,r_0,b_0`$ have exactly the definitions in Step 5 ($`S=ax^2+2x-2`$).

## A. Numerator expansion for the curvature equation

```math
T_1=\left(2 a x^{2} + x + 2\right)^{2}=4 a^{2} x^{4} + 4 a x^{3} + x^{2} \left(8 a + 1\right) + 4 x + 4.
```

```math
T_2=2 x \left(a x + 1\right) \left(4 a x + 1\right) \left(2 a x^{2} + x + 2\right)=16 a^{3} x^{5} + 28 a^{2} x^{4} + x^{3} \left(16 a^{2} + 14 a\right) + x^{2} \left(20 a + 2\right) + 4 x.
```

```math
T_3=\left(a x + 1\right)^{2} \left(- 8 a x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 8 x\right)=- 8 a^{3} x^{5} - 19 a^{2} x^{4} + x^{3} \left(8 a^{2} - 14 a\right) + x^{2} \left(16 a - 3\right) + 8 x.
```

Adding by powers of $`x`$ gives $`T_1+T_2+T_3=K`$; the coefficient sums are:

| Power | $`T_1`$ | $`T_2`$ | $`T_3`$ | Sum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | $`0`$ | $`16 a^{3}`$ | $`- 8 a^{3}`$ | $`8 a^{3}`$ |
| 4 | $`4 a^{2}`$ | $`28 a^{2}`$ | $`- 19 a^{2}`$ | $`13 a^{2}`$ |
| 3 | $`4 a`$ | $`16 a^{2} + 14 a`$ | $`8 a^{2} - 14 a`$ | $`4 a \left(6 a + 1\right)`$ |
| 2 | $`8 a + 1`$ | $`20 a + 2`$ | $`16 a - 3`$ | $`44 a`$ |
| 1 | $`4`$ | $`4`$ | $`8`$ | $`16`$ |
| 0 | $`4`$ | $`0`$ | $`0`$ | $`4`$ |

## C. Evaluated polynomial divisions for the critical and flat loci

For each pair below, use $`P_i=q_iP_{i+1}+c_iP_{i+2}`$ with the quotient, scalar factor and primitive remainder explicitly displayed. All equalities are rational identities in $`a`$; a zero denominator is handled by the final polynomial identity after denominators are cleared. No exceptional coupling is excluded on the basis of these computational divisions.

To track the resultant through a division, let $`m=\deg P_i`$, $`n=\deg P_{i+1}`$ and $`r=\deg P_{i+2}`$. Evaluating the division on the roots of $`P_{i+1}`$ gives $`P_i(\beta)=c_iP_{i+2}(\beta)`$. The leading-coefficient factors in the product definition then give

```math
\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}\nolimits(P_i,P_{i+1})=(-1)^{mn}\mathop{\mathrm{lc}}\nolimits(P_{i+1})^{m-r}c_i^n\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}\nolimits(P_{i+1},P_{i+2}),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Res}}\nolimits(P,c)=c^{\deg P}.
```

For the discriminant the product over root differences gives $`\mathop{\mathrm{Disc}}\nolimits Q=(-1)^{8\cdot7/2}\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}\nolimits(Q,Q_x)/\mathop{\mathrm{lc}}\nolimits Q=\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}\nolimits(Q,Q_x)/(352a^6)`$. The exponent is 28, hence the sign is positive.

## D. Flat reconstruction and critical-root multiplicity

For the flat case the degree-one remainder above solves for $`x`$. Reducing that rational solution modulo $`B`$ gives

```math
x_B=- \frac{2985472 a^{2}}{10137} - \frac{167888 a}{10137} + \frac{530015}{13516},\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{rem}}\nolimits_B Q(a,x_B)=0,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{rem}}\nolimits_B K(a,x_B)=0.
```

The critical final nonconstant subresultant has degree one in $`x`$ and its leading coefficient has gcd $`1`$ with $`\Delta`$. Therefore every root of that coupling polynomial has exactly one common $`x`$ root; the degree-two subresultant does not replace it with a higher-degree gcd.

Also $`\gcd(\Delta,\Delta\prime)=1`$. A triple Q root or two distinct double roots would produce at least a double zero of its discriminant; the simple Delta roots therefore have exactly one double Q root. The real-root count changes by two, so that double root is real.

The flat final nonconstant subresultant has degree one in $`x`$ and its leading coefficient has gcd $`1`$ with $`B`$. Therefore every root of that coupling polynomial has exactly one common $`x`$ root; the degree-two subresultant does not replace it with a higher-degree gcd.

Every sequence uses $`p_0=Q(a_*,x)`$, $`p_1=\partial_xp_0`$, $`p_{i+1}=-\mathop{\mathrm{rem}}\nolimits(p_{i-1},p_i)`$. We display each computed remainder after multiplication by a **positive** rational scalar, which preserves all signs and root counts. The actual division recurrence remains valid up to these displayed positive rescalings.

## F. Coupling-root isolations and limit balances

Exact disjoint rational intervals, each containing one simple real root, are:

| Polynomial | Lower bound | Upper bound | Root approximately |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | -100719/1683062 | -53974/901931 | -0.0598427152412957062 |
| Delta | 72736/86151 | 14204823/16824677 | 0.844285034416660494 |
| Delta | 86544497884/1557347 | 112516066311/2024699 | 55571.7498309625281 |
| B | -1276992/3356587 | -1210301/3181289 | -0.380443587489268960 |
| B | -59731/6100205 | -58801/6005226 | -0.00979163814985180649 |
| B | 375702/1097249 | 397811/1161819 | 0.342403592986122894 |

For Delta, the signs at negative/positive infinity are -+--+- and +++---; their variations differ by 4-1=3. The intervals above therefore exhaust the real roots.

For B, the signs at negative/positive infinity are -+-+ and ++++; their variations differ by 3-0=3. The intervals above therefore exhaust the real roots.

### Small compensator

```math
a \left(320 c - 24\right) - 216 a^{2} c + O\left(a^{3}\right)
```

### Square-root roots

```math
\frac{- 280 c^{3} + 320 c}{e} - 1720 c^{2} + 1700 c^{4} + O\left(e\right)
```

### Exceptional approach

```math
e^{6} \left(\frac{587 c^{6}}{16} - \frac{345 c^{4}}{2} + 324 c^{2} - 96\right) + O\left(e^{7}\right)
```

The leading coefficients set to zero are respectively $`320c-24`$, $`320c-280c^3`$ and $`(587c^6-2760c^4+5184c^2-1536)/16`$, giving precisely the root balances used in Step 5.
